evals.prompt: We're launching a new B2B SaaS product for design teams in 6 weeks. It's a design review tool. We have a small audience (500 email subscribers, 2k Twitter followers). Help us plan the launch.
evals.expected_output: Should check for product-marketing-context.md first. Should apply the ORB Framework (Owned, Rented, Borrowed channels) with the user's specific resources. Owned: email list (500 subscribers), website. Rented: Twitter (2k followers). Borrowed: partnerships, communities, Product Hunt. Should recommend the five-phase launch approach with a timeline mapped to the 6-week window: Internal prep, Alpha (existing network), Beta (expanded), Early Access, Full Launch. Should provide specific tactics for each phase. Should recommend building up the audience before launch day. Should include a launch day checklist.
assertions: Maps to user's specific channels and audience sizes
Provides specific tactics for each phase

evals.prompt: We want to launch on Product Hunt. Any tips? We've never done it before.
evals.expected_output: Should apply the Product Hunt strategy section. Should cover: choosing the right day and time, preparing assets (logo, gallery images, maker video), crafting the tagline and description, building a hunter network, activating supporters on launch day, engaging with comments, and post-launch follow-up. Should recommend preparation timeline (start 2-4 weeks before). Should mention common mistakes to avoid. Should set realistic expectations about outcomes.
assertions: Addresses hunter network and supporter activation

evals.prompt: we just shipped a major feature update. how should we announce it? it's not a full product launch, just a big new feature.
evals.expected_output: Should trigger on casual phrasing. Should apply the ongoing launch strategy section, specifically the major/medium/minor update matrix. Should identify this as a major feature update. Should recommend appropriate channels and tactics for a feature launch (less than a full product launch but more than a changelog entry). Should include: announcement email, blog post, social media push, in-app notification, and possibly a mini Product Hunt launch. Should provide a feature announcement framework.
assertions: Applies ongoing launch strategy / update matrix
Includes email, blog, social, and in-app notification

evals.prompt: Our launch flopped. We launched 3 weeks ago and only got 50 signups. We expected at least 500. What went wrong and what can we do now?
evals.expected_output: Should apply the post-launch product marketing section. Should diagnose potential failure causes: insufficient audience building pre-launch, wrong channels, weak value proposition messaging, poor launch execution, targeting the wrong audience. Should recommend post-launch recovery tactics: iterate on messaging, identify which channels produced the 50 signups and double down, try new distribution channels, leverage early users for testimonials. Should provide a specific 30-day recovery plan.
assertions: Suggests analyzing which channels produced signups

evals.prompt: How do we leverage partnerships and borrowed audiences for our launch? We don't have a big audience of our own.
evals.expected_output: Should focus on the Borrowed channel from the ORB Framework. Should provide specific borrowed audience tactics: podcast guest appearances, co-marketing with complementary tools, influencer partnerships, community engagement (relevant Slack groups, Discord servers, Reddit), guest posts, cross-promotions. Should recommend how to identify and approach potential partners. Should note that borrowed audience strategies take time to build and should start well before launch day.
assertions: Focuses on Borrowed channel from ORB Framework
Recommends how to identify and approach partners
Notes borrowed strategies take time to build
Suggests starting well before launch day

evals.prompt: Give me some creative marketing ideas to promote our product. We're bootstrapped and don't have a big budget.
evals.expected_output: Route ongoing GTM model and motion prioritization to go-to-market-strategy; optional tactics follow objectives, accepted audience, strategy and constraints.
assertions: Distinguishes ongoing GTM from release planning
Does not recommend tactics before objectives and constraints

evals.regression: single-segment proof narrowing (Stripe Radar GTM plan, 2026-09)
evals.prompt: Write the GTM plan for launching Tollgate, our fraud-screening API that blocks fraudulent card payments before authorization. Online payment fraud costs merchants about $200B a year across every industry (industry report we cite in sales decks). Our only published proof is from AI companies: three AI startup customers whose logos we can use, and a stat that they saw 38% fewer fraudulent free-trial signups. We have no case studies, stats, or logos outside AI. Phase 1 is the first 90 days. Phase 2 is months 4 to 12.
evals.expected_output: Should list the plausible segments from the cross-industry loss pool, not just AI companies, including segments with zero published proof, each labeled Sourced, Assumed, or Gap. Should size the full cross-industry market first, starting from the $200B figure, then the year-one wedge, without inventing sizes for unsized segments. Should pick a lead segment (AI companies is a valid lead) and explain why it goes first in 2 to 3 sentences, including that proof strength drove the choice if it did. Should give sequencing lines with triggers for the other segments. Segments must match in both directions across sizing, the Phase 2 plan, and the KPIs, or each exclusion must be stated with a reason. Should run a consistency check. Should rank Evidence gaps by impact on the main number or lead claim: top five in the body with why each matters, the rest in an appendix, each with an owner and resolve-by.
assertions: Lists at least two non-AI segments (for example marketplaces, e-commerce, SaaS, travel), each labeled Sourced, Assumed, or Gap
Sizes the full cross-industry market (from the $200B loss pool or an equivalent) before sizing the lead segment or year-one wedge
Gives a rationale for why the lead segment goes first, in 2 to 3 sentences that name the factors that drove the choice

Segments match in both directions across the market sizing, the Phase 2 plan (months 4 to 12), and the KPIs: every segment named in any one of the three appears in the other two, or the plan states why it is excluded from the one it is missing from

Has a ranked Evidence gaps section in the body listing the top five Assumed or Gap items with why each matters, and an appendix listing the remaining items in ranked order; every row has an owner and a resolve-by
Does not invent market sizes, stats, or customers for non-AI segments; unsized segments are labeled as gaps
